hero.headline: Murray Middle School students return to class in Stuart as tornado rebuild continues
hero.teaser: Murray Middle School students are returning to class this week in Stuart to a campus undergoing major construction nearly two years after a tornado destroyed two buildings and damaged a third.
hero.body:
Students at Murray Middle School in Stuart are returning to class this week to a campus where crews demolished two buildings over the summer and are rebuilding spaces for band, chorus, and agriculture programs. The October 2024 tornado spawned by Hurricane Milton destroyed two buildings and left a third with major roof damage. Those spaces housed the school's band, chorus, and agriculture programs. District leaders say the work zone is completely separated from the rest of campus, so students can learn safely while crews rebuild.

Superintendent Michael Maine said the programs never stopped despite the damage. Crews will build a new administration building and media center, plus modern spaces for band, chorus, and agriculture science. Crews will also renovate the gym.

The gym is expected to be finished by next August. The new administration building, media center, and specialized classrooms are expected to follow in December 2027. The project is being paid for through state support, insurance reimbursements, and district capital funds.

cards.body:
A crash on Interstate 95 southbound caused major delays Tuesday morning in Port St. Lucie near the Crosstown Parkway Exit. According to FL511, the crash was reported around 8:30 a.m. beyond Exit 120 for Crosstown Parkway, where two right lanes were blocked.

Fire trucks responded to the scene, narrowing traffic to one lane and causing a roughly two-mile backup. Drivers were urged to slow down or move over for emergency crews and Road Rangers working in the area.

The crash occurred as commuters navigated the morning rush hour on the major north-south corridor through St. Lucie County. The incident disrupted traffic flow on one of South Florida's busiest highways during peak travel times.

Officials reminded motorists to exercise caution when approaching the crash scene and to follow Florida's Move Over Law, which requires drivers to move over a lane or slow down when emergency vehicles are stopped on the roadside. The law applies to all emergency vehicles, including fire trucks and Road Ranger assistance vehicles responding to incidents on state highways.

cards.headline: Vindman's $14.5 million war chest leads Nixon ahead of Florida Democratic Senate primary
cards.teaser: Retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman and state Rep. Angie Nixon are presenting sharply contrasting campaigns in the Florida Democratic Senate primary, with Vindman holding a substantial f
cards.body:
Retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman and state Rep. Angie Nixon are presenting sharply contrasting campaigns in the Florida Democratic Senate primary, with Vindman holding a substantial fundraising advantage of roughly $14.5 million raised through June. The Aug. 18 primary will determine which Democrat challenges Republican Sen. Ashley Moody in November's general election to complete the final two years of a former senator's term.

Vindman has outpaced even Moody in fundraising and is highlighting his military service while positioning himself as a candidate capable of reaching voters beyond the Democratic base. He has focused his campaign on the November election and the need for congressional checks on President Donald Trump, saying Republicans in office have abandoned their responsibilities to check executive power. Vindman has declined to debate Nixon during the primary.

Nixon is countering Vindman's national profile with her Florida roots, a more progressive platform, and a working-class message centered on wages and affordability. The Jacksonville Democrat's campaign social-media posts have highlighted everyday challenges including car trouble and a flat tire, portraying those moments as evidence she deals with problems confronting voters. At the Florida Capitol, Nixon has developed a reputation as an outspoken protester, using a bullhorn during the fight over Florida's congressional maps and facing charges following a sit-in demonstration at the governor's office.

Moody faces three lower-profile candidates in the Republican primary but is expected to advance easily to November, allowing her to concentrate on the general election. She is framing the race as a choice between Republicans and Democrats moving the country toward socialism and greater government control. The latest Decision Desk HQ polling average gives Moody a seven-point advantage over Vindman, 47% to 40%, placing the race within competitive territory though not yet a top-tier national toss-up. The winner in November will serve the remainder of the term and must run again in 2028 for a full six-year term.

cards.headline: Mets, Tortugas split Saturday doubleheader as Zayas powers Game 1 win
cards.teaser: Julio Zayas hit a go-ahead three-run homer for the second straight day, lifting St. Lucie to a 3-1 win before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets and Daytona Tortugas split a Saturday doubleheader at Clover Park, with the Mets taking the opener 3-1 before Daytona answered with a 15-7 victory in Game 2.

The split left the seven-game series tied 3-3 heading into Sunday’s finale. It was also the second time the teams split a doubleheader during the series after each club won once during Wednesday’s twin bill.

## Zayas delivers another go-ahead home run

Julio Zayas provided the biggest swing for St. Lucie in Game 1, hitting a go-ahead three-run home run in the fourth inning to erase a 1-0 Daytona lead.

The homer came one night after Zayas hit a walk-off home run in the bottom of the ninth inning Friday. Saturday’s blast was his third home run of the series.

St. Lucie’s pitching staff made the lead hold up.

Starter Nate Hall worked the first 1 2/3 innings before Caden Wooster took over. Wooster allowed Daytona’s only run when Arnaldo Lantigua hit a solo home run in the third inning.

Ernesto Mercedes followed with two scoreless innings, allowing four hits while striking out three to earn the win.

Miguel Mijias recorded the final five outs for his fourth save of the season, including a perfect seventh inning to close the game.

The Mets held Daytona to 1-for-8 with runners in scoring position and stranded 10 Tortugas runners.

The performance continued a sharp turnaround for St. Lucie’s pitching staff. From the ninth inning of Thursday’s game through the end of Saturday’s opener, the Mets allowed only one run after Daytona had scored 17 runs over the first eight innings Thursday.

Daytona starter Dusty Revis was charged with the loss despite throwing a six-inning complete game on just 63 pitches. Revis allowed five hits and three earned runs while becoming the first Tortugas pitcher since 2019 to record a complete game.

Elian Peña went 1-for-3 for St. Lucie and extended his hitting streak to 10 games.

## Daytona pulls away in Game 2

The nightcap was a much different game, with Daytona breaking a 6-6 tie during a decisive fifth inning.

Mets newcomer Wilmer Lugo appeared to escape the inning by striking out Henry Hunter looking on a 3-2 pitch. Hunter challenged the call using the ABS system, however, and the ruling was overturned to ball four, loading the bases.

Lugo then walked the next two hitters to force home a pair of runs. After Luis Sotillo entered in relief, a wild pitch allowed Hunter to score and stretched Daytona’s lead to 9-6.

Hunter delivered another major blow in the seventh inning, hitting a grand slam off Sotillo to push the Tortugas ahead 13-6.

For the second time in four games, the Mets eventually turned to Zayas to finish the game on the mound as a position player. He recorded the final four outs, allowing a two-run homer to Drew Davies with two outs in the seventh but no additional damage.

Logan Tanner earned the win for Daytona after throwing two scoreless innings of relief.

St. Lucie still produced several offensive highlights in the loss.

Simon Juan went 2-for-3 with a double and his ninth home run of the season.

Kuhio Aloy, the Mets’ 11th-round draft pick, hit a two-run homer in the third inning to tie the game at 6-6. It was Aloy’s first professional home run.

Lugo took the loss after being charged with three runs on one hit and four walks over 2/3 of an inning.

## Series finale set for Sunday

The Mets fell to 16-24 in the second half and 49-57 overall, while Daytona improved to 25-14 in the second half and 46-60 overall.

St. Lucie and Daytona will decide the series Sunday at Clover Park, with first pitch scheduled for 12:10 p.m.

Sunday is Little League Day. Little leaguers who attend wearing their team jerseys will receive free admission courtesy of Holiday Inn Express.

hero.body:
A crash on Interstate 95 southbound caused major delays Tuesday morning in Port St. Lucie near the Crosstown Parkway Exit. According to FL511, the crash was reported around 8:30 a.m. beyond Exit 120 for Crosstown Parkway, where two right lanes were blocked.

Fire trucks responded to the scene, narrowing traffic to one lane and causing a roughly two-mile backup. Drivers were urged to slow down or move over for emergency crews and Road Rangers working in the area.

The crash occurred as commuters navigated the morning rush hour on the major north-south corridor through St. Lucie County. The incident disrupted traffic flow on one of South Florida's busiest highways during peak travel times.

Officials reminded motorists to exercise caution when approaching the crash scene and to follow Florida's Move Over Law, which requires drivers to move over a lane or slow down when emergency vehicles are stopped on the roadside. The law applies to all emergency vehicles, including fire trucks and Road Ranger assistance vehicles responding to incidents on state highways.
